unit.unitinstructions:
Informed Consent Form

Title of the Study

The Effect of Flashcard Quality and Adaptive Practice Scheduling on Vocabulary Learning

Researchers

The person in charge of this study is Hannah-Joy Simms of the University of Memphis, Department of Psychology. She is being guided in this research by Dr. Philip I. Pavlik Jr. There may be other people on the research team assisting at different times during the study.

Contact Information

If you should have any questions about this research, please feel free to contact Hannah-Joy Simms at hsimms1@memphis.edu or 901-267-2983; Philip Pavlik Jr. (faculty advisor) at ppavlik@memphis.edu or 901-678-2326.

For questions regarding the research subjects’ rights, the Chair of the Institutional Review Board for the Protection of Human Subjects should be contacted at irb@memphis.edu or 901-678-2705.

Key information for you to consider

You are being invited to participate in a research study. The purpose of this study is to evaluate how flashcard design, instructional strategy, and scheduling method affect vocabulary learning. This research uses adaptive learning techniques to investigate how people remember new Russian vocabulary. You are invited to participate because you are an experienced Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) worker. A total of 260 individuals will take part in this study. If you agree to participate, you will be asked to complete the following:The experiment consists of two parts. The first part involves a short instructional video, a brief reading passage introducing vocabulary in context, and flashcard-based practice using a system called MoFaCTS. This session will take approximately 40 minutes.The second part will take place 1 day later and includes a post-test (about 20 minutes) with the same vocabulary items as well as a short survey (about 10 minutes).During the first session, you will watch a short video introducing the strategies used for learning, read a brief text containing Russian words you will later study, study vocabulary using digital flashcards with varying formats (e.g., keywords, images, audio), practice typing the correct Russian word when prompted with the English translation, and complete a short survey. In the second session, you will be shown each Russian word (e.g., девочка) and asked to type the correct English translation (e.g., girl). You will then complete a short follow-up survey.Participation in this study is voluntary. You may withdraw at any time without penalty. You may also skip any questions or parts of the study.There are no known risks beyond typical online activity (e.g., eyestrain or brief frustration). However, participation may help you improve memory strategies and contribute to educational research.Upon completion of the research study, you will receive compensation. You will be paid $5.00 for completing the first part and $3.00 for completing the second part. You can also earn a bonus of $0.12 for each correct response during the first session (up to 30 bonus-eligible responses). It is important to note that the bonus, along with the second session payment, will only be paid if you return and complete the full second session, including the survey. All efforts, within the limits allowed by law, will be made to keep the personal information (your Amazon Turk Worker ID) in your research record private, but total privacy cannot be promised. We will deidentify your data (remove your ID) after the experiment before storing it long-term. Worker IDs will only be used to distribute payment and will not be stored with survey responses or research data. MTurk Worker IDs will not be shared with anyone. Further identifying information we gather (e.g., demographic information or IP addresses) will never be attached to your responses.If you have questions about the research, you may contact Hannah-Joy Simms at hsimms1@memphis.edu or Philip Pavlik at ppavlik@memphis.edu or 901-678-2326. For questions regarding the research subjects’ rights, the Chair of the Institutional Review Board for the Protection of Human Subjects may be contacted at 901-678-2705 or irb@memphis.edu.

Confidentiality

All efforts, within the limits allowed by law, will be made to keep the personal information (your Amazon Turk Worker ID) in your research record private. However, there may be unexpected extenuating circumstances, such that total privacy cannot be promised. We will de-identify your data (remove your ID) after the experiment before storing it on our computers long-term. By participating, you understand and agree that the de-identified data gathered during this study may be used by the University of Memphis and published and/or disclosed by the University of Memphis to others outside of the University of Memphis. However, no personally identifying information will ever be mentioned in any such publication or dissemination of the research data and/or results to other researchers.

Other notes

Amazon.com has stated that the MTurk platform is NOT meant to support participant anonymity. MTurk worker IDs are linked to Amazon.com's public profiles. Amazon.com may disclose worker information. Additionally, worker information may be available to others (who submit a request) for tax reporting purposes.

ELECTRONIC CONSENT

I have had the opportunity to consider the information in this document. I have asked any questions needed for me to decide about my participation. I understand that I can ask additional questions through the study. You may print a copy of this consent document for your records. Clicking on the Continue button indicates that you:

  • Have read the above information
  • Voluntarily agree to participate
  • Are 18 years of age or older

First, please put on your headphones.

On the next screen you will read a brief passage for 5 minutes. Important Russian vocabulary words appear bolded with a small speaker icon 🔊 immediately after them. Click the icon to hear the pronunciation of the word as many times as you like.

Please press the CONTINUE button below.

With осень (fall) came дождь (rain), and it quickly covered the ground with puddles.

I ran to the house and pulled the дверь (door) closed, and saw народ (people) already seated around the table.

The пир (feast) smelled amazing! On the table there was a стакан (glass) of hot чай (tea), some имбирь (ginger), slices of ветчина (ham), and some unfinished тесто (dough) for bread.

My муж (husband) was already inside waiting. I recognized him by his bright blue костюм (suit) he always wears. I could still see the stitch where I fixed his sleeve with a игла (needle).

I wiped my feet on the ковёр (carpet) and used a towel to remove the water from my dress. Even though I was late, we laughed a lot and soon my рот (mouth) felt a little боль (pain) from smiling.

I even played with my little cousins in the yard. Near the step, a small жаба (toad) sat. We tried to poke it with a карандаш (pencil), then a мяч (ball), and finally my сумка (bag) before it hopped away.

We said goodbye and drove home. From the window, I watched the закат (sunset), then I saw a лошадь (horse) walking slowly.

When we got home, our собака (dog) ran across the yard, leaving a след (track) of paws in the wet поле (field).

We walked to the river and sat on a big скала (rock) near the lake. Far out on the water, we thought we saw a акула (shark). But, when I closed my left глаз (eye) to make sure, it was just a boat with a white парус (sail).

Later, I had a calm сон (dream).

Please watch the following video about learning strategies. The video will pause automatically at key points for embedded questions-answer each one correctly to continue. If you answer incorrectly, the video will replay the previous section. If there are any loading issues with the video, please refresh the page. Thank you!

In this 20-minute training session, you will engage in flashcard practice of Russian vocabulary.Please make an effort to learn the items and provide accurate responses.

The Russian target word and the corresponding English meaning will be displayed for 7 seconds. Your task is to memorize the English meaning for each Russian word. Afterwards, the Russian word will be shown, and you will be asked to type the corresponding English meaning within a 10-second timeframe in the provided blank. Press ENTER after each response or if you are unable to make a guess.

If you provide an incorrect response for the item, you will have a 6-second opportunity to review the answer. In the case of a correct response, the feedback will only be displayed for 1 second.

You will know that you have continued correctly when you observe the final page of part 1, which you have previously encountered.
  To proceed, please follow this link to Part 2: https://staging.optimallearning.org/experiment/flashcardtest
 We appreciate your participation in this study.
Best regards,
Hannah-Joy and Phil
